Introduction

HIGH4 was a South Korean boy group under N.A.P Entertainment. The group debuted on April 8, 2014 with the single “Not Spring, Love, or Cherry Blossoms,” a collaboration with IU that became a major success and introduced the members to the public. Following their debut, the group continued to promote with songs such as “Headache,” “Day by Day,” and “D.O.A,” building a reputation for their bright pop sound paired with strong vocal and rap performances.

The group was originally composed of four members: Sung Gu, Alex, Myunghan, and Youngjun. Over the course of their activities, they held promotions both in South Korea and Japan, gradually expanding their international fanbase. On February 13, 2017, it was announced that leader Sung Gu had requested to leave the group. N.A.P Entertainment stated that the company would decide the group’s direction after the conclusion of their Japanese promotions in March of that year.

Later in 2017, on August 16, Alex confirmed during an Instagram live broadcast that the members had gone their separate ways and would focus on individual pursuits. This announcement effectively confirmed the disbandment of HIGH4, bringing their group activities to an end after three years.
